title: Coherence and imaginarity of qubit states under vanishing Bargmann invariants
abstract: Set coherence and set imaginarity are two important quantum resources defined by sets of states. We investigate tuples of qubit states under vanishing higher-order Bargmann invariants and show that their set coherence and set imaginarity are each related to whether they contain a pair of orthogonal states. Specifically, when the relevant higher-order Bargmann invariants vanish, the tuple contains a pair of orthogonal states if and only if removing some state makes the remaining tuple incoherent. Moreover, when maximally mixed states are excluded, the same vanishing conditions imply that the tuple is imaginarity-free if and only if it contains a pair of orthogonal states. As a consequence, under these conditions, a tuple of single-qubit states has imaginarity precisely when every tuple obtained by deleting one of its states is coherent.
summary: This theoretical paper establishes strong equivalences between set coherence, set imaginarity, and the presence of orthogonal pairs among a set of single-qubit states. These equivalences hold specifically when higher-order Bargmann invariants vanish. The findings provide a powerful diagnostic tool, linking abstract algebraic constraints on state products to fundamental geometric properties of the state set.
main_problem: The paper investigates the deep mathematical relationship between set coherence, set imaginarity, and the existence of orthogonal pairs among a set of single-qubit states.
main_result: Under the vanishing of higher-order Bargmann invariants, the set coherence and set imaginarity of the qubit states are equivalent to the existence of at least one pair of orthogonal states within the set.
method: The analysis employs algebraic techniques involving the cyclicity of the trace, the Bloch vector representation, and inductive proofs based on the vanishing of multivariate traces (Bargmann invariants).
model_or_system: The system under study consists of an $n$-tuple of single-qubit density operators ($ho_i \in D(\mathbb{C}^2)$). The properties are analyzed using constraints derived from higher-order traces of these operators.
key_observables: Set coherence, set imaginarity, pairwise orthogonality ($	ext{Tr}(ho_iho_j) = 0$), and higher-order Bargmann invariants ($\Delta_w(\vec{ho})$).
important_parameters: The number of states $n$ (analyzed for $n \ge 4$), and the condition that maximally mixed states are excluded for imaginarity results.
main_assumptions: The results rely heavily on the vanishing of specific higher-order traces (Bargmann invariants) and, for some theorems, the assumption that $	ext{Tr}(ho_k^2) > 1/2$.
paper_structure: The paper develops results by first establishing equivalences for set coherence (related to commutativity) and then for set imaginarity (related to real representations), culminating in a combined corollary showing the equivalence of all three conditions under the vanishing invariant constraints.
why_interesting: This work provides powerful, necessary and sufficient conditions (based on simple geometric properties like orthogonality) for complex quantum resource measures (coherence/imaginarity) to vanish, which is crucial for understanding quantum state characterization.
